nodes.name: Webhook - ado-event
nodes.notes: ADO Service Hook payload arrives here. ADO can send Basic Auth on the webhook (configured in the ADO subscription); n8n verifies against the jytte-internal-basic credential (username 'jytte', password = env.JYTTE_INTERNAL_SECRET). Register that credential once in n8n UI - separate from ado-pat because auth flows opposite way here.

nodes.name: Route by eventType
nodes.notes: ADO event types we care about: git.pullrequest.merged fires on PR completion (whether to dev or main - we look at target branch to disambiguate). ms.vss-pipelines.run-state-changed-event fires on pipeline run state transitions; we filter to 'completed' + result in the shape node.

nodes.name: POST Teams webhook
nodes.notes: TEAMS_WEBHOOK_TWAPP_SHIPPING env var is the Incoming Webhook URL configured in the target Teams channel (Channel settings -> Manage channel -> Connectors -> Incoming Webhook).

parameters.responseBody: ={"status":"skipped","reason":"filtered out (target != dev/main OR pipeline state != completed)"}

meta.description: Receives ADO Service Hook webhooks (git.pullrequest.merged, ms.vss-pipelines.run-state-changed-event), filters to interesting subsets (target dev/main; pipeline state completed), compiles a Teams AdaptiveCard v1.4, and POSTs to TEAMS_WEBHOOK_TWAPP_SHIPPING (a Power Automate 'Post card in a chat or channel' workflow URL). Auth via Basic Auth on the webhook node (jytte-internal-basic credential). Container.style drives the color band: accent=dev, warning=main, good=pipeline success, attention=pipeline failure.
